viNames.name: Cá vàng lan thọ (widely used, though some say this name belongs to Ranchu)

origin.fact: Bred in China to look like the mythical Chinese lion-dog.
Reached Japan in the 17th–18th centuries. There it was the precursor of the Ranchu, which Japanese breeders gave a rounder back, a different tail and a smaller head growth.
Comes from the Egg Fish (Maruko), a fantail without a dorsal fin that is linked to the twin-tailed Wakin.
Chinese names refer to the mythical stone lion. Japanese names are Shishi and Kara Shishi.
Described as the Chinese counterpart of the Japanese ranchu.

looks.fact: No dorsal fin. Short, deep body with a fairly straight or evenly arched back.
A raspberry-like hood (wen) should cover the top of the head, the gill plates and the cheeks evenly. Hoods only on the cap ('goose-head') or only on the cheeks are judged inferior.
Body depth should be about half of body length. The back should be smooth, with no bumps, dips or dorsal spikes.
The double tail should be forked, even and held above horizontal. Breed standards also call for paired anal fins.
Compared with the ranchu, it has a flatter back and peduncle, a tail held more level, a rounded rather than rectangular head growth and a shorter body.
Males usually grow bigger hoods and periodically shed patches of it.
Scales are metallic, nacreous or matt. Colours include red, white, red-and-white, blue, black, black-and-white, black-and-red, natural and chocolate.

Vietnamese judging: the wen should cover the crown, face and gill covers evenly. The back should be nearly flat with only a slight curve near the tail base. The tail lobes should be split by more than 25%, ideally over 50%.

lines.fact: Lionchu: a Thai cross of lionhead and ranchu, known in Vietnam as cá vàng lan sư.
Lionchu can be told apart by its high back, rounded tail and large crest. A curved back with a sharply bent tail suggests a ranchu instead.
Scale-type forms: metallic (the most popular), matt, and nacreous or calico.

keeping.fact: Needs at least 70 L for one fish plus about 45 L for each extra goldfish, with a filter turning the water over about 4 times an hour but without strong current, since it swims weakly.
Keep decor sparse and smooth. Avoid sharp items and gaps a fish could get stuck in, and keep the tank out of direct sun.
Suggested water hardness is GH 11 dGH or more and KH 8 dKH or more. Ammonia and nitrite should be zero and nitrate under 30 ppm.
Usually needs no heater indoors. Pond fish should come indoors if it stays below 7°C for a long time.
Feed gel food plus frozen or live foods such as bloodworm, daphnia and brine shrimp, at about 1–2% of body weight a day, with enough vegetable matter.
Do not keep with fast single-tailed goldfish, which take the food. Plecos and bristlenose may graze on its slime coat.
Vietnamese practice: shallow water of 15–25 cm (deep water can make the tail droop), an air stone, gentle flow, and frequent partial changes with aged, chlorine-free water.

breeding.fact: Can be crossed with ranchu, giving the lionchu.
Does not breed true for the missing dorsal fin. Getting 40% of fry without a dorsal fin is considered a very good result, so fry are culled when dorsal fins appear.
Breeding nacreous fish gives roughly 50% nacreous, 25% matt and 25% metallic fry.
The hood starts growing about 120 days after hatching and can take 4–5 years to mature.

health.fact: The short body makes it more prone to swim bladder disorders than the longer ranchu.
The deep body can lead to buoyancy problems on poor food or too little plant matter.
The hood can grow over the eyes and may need trimming.
Like other goldfish it gets flukes, ich, Costia, anchor worm, fin rot, gill disease and carp pox. Quarantine new fish.

buying.fact: Choose fish whose wen covers all three areas evenly, whose back is fairly straight and whose double tail is well split.
Avoid fish with a dorsal fin ridge or a tapered tail base.
Avoid fish with bumps or spikes on the back. Black patches on metallic fish usually mean injury or a colour change still in progress.
Names are mixed up in Vietnam: 'lan thọ' may be used for both lionhead and ranchu, so check the back and tail shape yourself.

controversy.fact: The animal-welfare charity UFAW lists excessive facial tissue in lionheads as a genetic welfare problem from selective breeding, and notes that the missing dorsal fin impairs swimming.
